title: How to Reopen Closed-Lost Deals in HubSpot (Without Bad Data)
summary: How to reopen closed-lost deals in HubSpot: when to move the stage back, when to clone, what it does to your reports, and how to lock it down.
body_markdown:
## How to reopen a closed-lost deal in HubSpot


Open the deal record and change Deal stage from Closed lost to an open stage, or drag the card out of the Closed lost column on the board. Then update Close date, Amount and the next step. HubSpot doesn’t document resetting the close date when you reopen, so set it yourself or the forecast keeps the old one.


The harder question is whether to reopen at all. Reopen the original deal only when:


- The loss was recent, usually within the same quarter
- It was lost on timing, and they didn’t pick someone else
- The same buyers came back to the same project


For everything else, clone it. On the deal record, click Actions, then Clone, and associate the new deal with the old one. The lost deal stays lost, and the new attempt gets its own history.


## What reopening does to your reports


Moving a deal out of Closed lost rewrites history in four places:


- **Win-loss numbers.** Is closed lost is true only while the deal sits in a lost stage. Move it back and the property flips to false, so the loss disappears from the period it happened in.
- **Cycle time.** Days to close runs from Create date to Close date. A deal lost, revived 100 days later and won 30 days after that reads as a 130-day cycle.
- **Close date.** HubSpot sets it when a deal enters a closed stage, and its documentation doesn’t say it resets on reopen. Fix it by hand.
- **Deal scores.** HubSpot’s documentation says reopened deals do not receive a deal score, and it recommends creating a new deal instead.


If anyone reports win rate or cycle length to leadership, default to cloning.


## How to clone a closed-lost deal instead


HubSpot has a native clone action for deals on all plans. Older community threads that say you need custom code are out of date.


1. Open the closed-lost deal.
2. In the upper right of the left sidebar, click Actions, then Clone.
3. Review the panel, which mirrors the create-deal form.
4. Set a new stage, close date and amount, then click Clone.


Property values and associations copy over. Activities, quotes and attachments do not, and unique properties are cleared.


Two habits keep clones useful:


- **Label them.** HubSpot sets Record source to Record Clone on every clone, and you can filter on it in a segment. Add a custom “Re-engaged deal” checkbox too, so you can report revived deals separately from net-new pipeline.
- **Leave the original alone.** Keep its Closed lost reason as it was. Your win-loss analysis depends on it, and it is the first thing a rep should read before reaching back out.


## Stop reps from reopening deals on their own


If reps can drag deals out of Closed lost, some will. HubSpot gives admins two controls.


**Pipeline rules** need a Professional or Enterprise plan and a Super Admin to set up. Go to Settings, then Data Management, then Objects, pick Deals, open the Pipelines tab, choose the pipeline and click Pipeline Rules. Turn on the editing-access rule for the Closed lost stage and limit it to super admins or specific users and teams.


The “Restrict deals from moving backwards” rule won’t stop this on its own, because HubSpot still lets users move a deal back out of a closed stage when they reopen it. Use the editing-access rule. Super admins, users who can edit property settings, workflows and the API can all bypass pipeline rules.


**Conditional stage properties** work on Starter and up. In the same Pipelines tab, edit the Closed lost stage’s properties, add Closed lost reason and tick Required. If Closed lost reason is free text in your account, you can’t segment it. Make it a dropdown first, with values like “chose a competitor”, “timing or budget”, “no decision” and “price”. You’ll filter on those later when you pick which lost deals to go back to.


## What to do with the contacts after a loss


Losing the deal does nothing to the contacts. HubSpot leaves their lifecycle stage at Opportunity. If your marketing emails exclude opportunities, the people you sold to drop out of every program.


You have three options:


- **Roll them back to lead or MQL.** They get marketing email again, but MQL content ignores that they already went through a sales cycle, and your MQL-to-opportunity conversion rate changes.
- **Leave them as Opportunity.** Conversion numbers stay clean, but someone has to write separate emails for them.
- **Move them to Other.** This is usually a poor fit, since most teams use Other for partners, competitors and employees.


Whichever you pick, add a custom property, such as a checkbox or a rollback date, so marketing can find these contacts and write to them as people who already know you.


## What should trigger a reopen


Reopen when buying activity resumes. Good triggers:


- Budget came back after a freeze
- A new decision-maker restarted the project
- The vendor they chose is coming up for renewal
- The account is evaluating vendors in your category again


Bad triggers are an opened marketing email, a downloaded guide, or a rep who wants another shot.


On our calls, lost deals come back more often than the Closed lost stage suggests. When teams first cross-check accounts that are actively evaluating competitors against their CRM, some of those accounts turn out to be closed-lost deals back in a buying cycle. Closed-lost deals sit outside most daily views, so nobody had noticed.


When you reach back out, skip “who else are you looking at?” Buyers keep their other evaluations to themselves and you’ll get a polite non-answer. Play back the problem you learned the first time, then ask how they’re solving it today: building in-house, doing nothing, or looking at vendors. Better still, know which vendors are in the room before you call.


## Make revival triggers something reps act on


Plenty of triggers land in HubSpot and never get worked. Three patterns we hear from sales leaders:


- **Vague alerts get ignored.** We’ve seen a closed-lost account flagged as evaluating competitors get no outreach at all, because the field explaining the flag was a vague summary. Reps didn’t know why it mattered or what to say. Spell it out in the record: which roles at the account are active, and which vendors they’re evaluating.
- **Closed-lost competes with everything else.** Reps are often handed several new signal types at once. A revival trigger with no owner loses to whatever leadership is pushing that month. Give it a named owner and a weekly routine.
- **Not every revival needs a rep.** One team swept its deferred and closed-lost accounts into an automated campaign timed to next quarter’s budget planning, instead of waiting for reps to reopen them one by one.
